---
title: "Scene flow"
subtitle: "Nine scenes, and the same two calls you learned in lesson 7."
---

*Cold Chain* has five scenes. *Snail Assassin* has nine:

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 9
flowchart LR
  B[Boot] --> SP[Splash] --> T[Title]
  T --> SE[Settings] --> T
  T --> SL[Select]
  SL --> H[Hunt]
  H -.->|launch + pause| P[Pause]
  P -.->|resume| H
  H -->|start| R[Results]
  R --> D["Discovery<br/>Did you know?"]
  R --> H
  D --> T
```

| Scene | Job | *Cold Chain* equivalent |
|---|---|---|
| `Boot` | Draw every sprite in code, then pick the first scene | `Boot` |
| `Splash` | The studio logo | none |
| `Title` | The menu | `Title` |
| `Settings` | Volume, text size, accessibility, key remapping | none |
| `Select` | Choose one of three snails | none |
| `Hunt` | The game itself | `Play` (+ `Hud`) |
| `Pause` | Overlay with options | [exercise 7.1](../lessons/07-scenes.qmd#exercises) |
| `Results` | Won or lost, with stats | `Results` |
| `Discovery` | The science behind your snail | none |

## Boot draws the art

{{< snippet repo="minus80" file="snail-assassin/src/scenes/BootScene.ts" method="makeTexture" >}}

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}
There are no image files at all. `Boot` draws each sprite with a `Graphics` object (rectangles and circles, pixel by pixel), then `generateTexture` turns the drawing into a texture with a key, exactly as if it had been loaded from a PNG. The comment at the top of the scene says why: these are placeholders, and real art can replace them later under the same keys without touching any other scene.

*Cold Chain* does the same thing one step earlier: its art is drawn by a Python script into PNG files. Both are ways to have a playable game before anyone has drawn anything.
:::

## Jumping to a scene

{{< snippet repo="minus80" file="snail-assassin/src/scenes/BootScene.ts" method="devStart" >}}

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}
In development only (`import.meta.env.DEV`), `?scene=Hunt&char=catalyst` skips the splash, the title and the menu. When you're tuning the hunt, that saves dozens of clicks an hour. In the built game this code still exists, but the `DEV` check is always false, so it always starts at the splash.
:::

## Pause, the lesson 7 way

{{< snippet repo="minus80" file="snail-assassin/src/scenes/HuntScene.ts" method="pauseHunt" >}}

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}
`launch` the overlay, `pause` the hunt: the same two calls as [exercise 7.1](../answers/07-scenes-answers.qmd#ex-7.1), and the opposite of the [bug in 7.3](../answers/07-scenes-answers.qmd#ex-7.3). The pause screen passes data in (`characterId`) the same way `start` does.
:::

## Ending a hunt

{{< snippet repo="minus80" file="snail-assassin/src/scenes/HuntScene.ts" method="finish" >}}

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}
An `ended` flag so it only happens once, a sound, a short delay so the moment lands, then `start('Results', {...})` with everything the results screen needs. Compare *Cold Chain*'s `Play.finish()`: same steps, same reasons. The difference is the amount of data passed: the results screen here shows venom spent and which fish you caught, so `Hunt` hands all of it over rather than leaving it in the registry.
:::
